questions.question: A 95% confidence interval for a mean is built from...
questions.explanation: Every confidence interval is estimate ± (critical value × standard error).

questions.question: Which critical value z* goes with 95% confidence?
questions.explanation: 1.96 leaves 2.5% in each tail of the standard normal curve. (1.645 is for 90%, and 2.576 is for 99%.)

questions.question: σ = 12, n = 40, x̄ = 78.5. What is the 95% confidence interval?
Keeping everything else fixed, what happens to the interval if you switch from 95% to 99% confidence?
questions.explanation: A higher confidence level needs a larger critical value (2.576 vs 1.96), which widens the interval. More certainty costs precision.

questions.question: How must n change to halve the margin of error?
questions.explanation: The margin is proportional to 1/√n. Halving it requires √n to double, so n must be four times as large.

questions.question: Which is the correct reading of a 95% CI of (74.78, 82.22) for the mean exam score?
options: We are 95% confident the true mean score lies between 74.78 and 82.22
The sample mean has a 95% chance of being 78.5
95% of future samples will have means in this range
questions.explanation: The interval is about the population mean, not individual scores or future sample means. The 95% describes the long-run success rate of the method.
